playbook.claim: The observed article recommends choosing the single bottleneck most limiting results, then concentrating on it for 30 days instead of improving multiple channels at once.
playbook.mechanism: Force a weekly growth review to identify one measurable bottleneck, freeze unrelated experiments, and run one focused 30-day intervention with a before/after metric.

playbook.claim: The observed article describes a short-form funnel that starts with a specific pain, gives a small insight or solution, then offers a free self-check delivered through an owned channel.
playbook.mechanism: Create content around a narrowly recognizable problem; teach one diagnostic distinction; invite viewers to complete a relevant free check or receive a tool in the owned channel, measuring view-to-click and click-to-completion rates.

playbook.claim: The observed article treats Pinterest content as durable search assets: select one theme, enumerate concrete user problems, and expand successful content into multiple distinct search intents.
playbook.mechanism: Choose one audience theme, list 30 situation-based problems, publish one useful asset per intent, and expand only the intents receiving saves or clicks into adjacent variants rather than duplicating the original.

playbook.claim: The observed article says repeated business decisions should be encoded as saved loops so weekly testing, killing, fixing, and scaling decisions compound instead of being recreated in disconnected chats.
playbook.mechanism: Maintain a versioned decision brief containing current hypotheses, test outcomes, stop rules, and next actions; require every new content or acquisition cycle to update that brief before generating the next batch.

playbook.claim: The observed Japanese relationship-app storefront treatment combines an upfront free-point offer, anonymous use, prepaid spending control, verified providers, reviews, and a three-step provider-selection explanation.
playbook.mechanism: Test a storefront and onboarding sequence that leads with low-risk access, privacy, spend control, provider trust signals, and a simple three-step path; compare it against feature-led copy using product-page conversion as the primary metric.
